items.title: Catenary
paragraphs: Cosh is even, so the curve is symmetric about the y-axis. Since cosh≥1, y≥a; the y-intercept is (0,a) and there is no x-intercept or passage through the origin.
\(y\prime=\sinh(x/a)\): the curve decreases for x<0, has a horizontal tangent at zero and increases for x>0.
\(y^{\prime\prime}=\cosh(x/a)/a>0\), so it is concave upwards throughout. There are no straight-line asymptotes. The supplied notes contain no catenary drawing.
items.final_answer: A y-axis-symmetric curve with minimum a at (0,a), concave upwards.
